application.name: ofetch / $fetch HTTP client
application.summary: The repository appears to be the TypeScript `ofetch` library: a typed, JSON-first wrapper around platform `fetch`. It provides request option merging, automatic body serialization, content-type-based response parsing, lifecycle hooks, timeout/abort handling, retries, normalized errors, and runtime-specific entrypoints for global/browser-like environments and Node.js.
application.purpose: Give application code a single ergonomic HTTP client callable, `$fetch`/`ofetch`, with safer defaults and typed responses while remaining injectable and runtime-compatible.

domains.name: Request/response lifecycle
domains.description: Resolves defaults and per-call options, merges headers/query, serializes bodies, applies base URLs, parses responses, and invokes hooks.

domains.name: Retry, timeout, and abort behavior
domains.description: Handles timeout via AbortController, retryable status codes, retry delays, and abort-aware error paths.

domains.name: Error normalization
domains.description: Converts request/response failures into `FetchError` instances carrying request, options, response, status, and data metadata.

domains.name: Runtime adaptation
domains.description: Provides global entrypoint exports and a Node-specific adapter with optional keep-alive agents.

domains.name: Extensibility
domains.description: Supports lifecycle hooks and configurable `create()` instances with merged defaults.

terminology.meaning: Main callable HTTP client. `$fetch` returns parsed response data; `.raw` returns the full response object; `.native` delegates to native fetch; `.create` creates a configured client instance.
Per-request state containing request, resolved options, optional response, and optional error.
Request configuration including baseURL, query/params, body, responseType, parseResponse, retry settings, timeout, and hooks.
Lifecycle extension points: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError. They may be single functions or arrays.
HTTP methods treated as capable of carrying a request body: PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE.
Parser selection such as json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream.
Normalized application-facing error type with request, response, status, statusText, data, and related aliases attached.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Core factory and orchestrator for the `$fetch` client. It defines the request lifecycle, injects runtime fetch/Headers/AbortController, applies defaults, serializes request bodies, parses responses, invokes hooks, and delegates failures to retry/error handling.

Internal resilience policy for failed requests. It determines whether a request should be retried, applies retry delay, and otherwise throws a normalized FetchError. The graph shows it depends on payload-method detection and error creation.

Translates a FetchContext into a user-facing FetchError. It builds an error message from method, URL, status, and underlying error, and attaches request/response/status/data fields for debugging and handling.
Encodes HTTP body semantics: identifies PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE as methods that can carry request payloads. This affects retry defaults and whether JSON body serialization/header handling applies.

Decides whether a request body should be treated as JSON-serializable. It excludes non-JSON bodies such as streams, buffers, FormData, and URLSearchParams, separating automatic JSON handling from native body passthrough.
Infers the correct response parser from the response Content-Type header, defaulting to JSON and distinguishing event streams, text-like content, and binary/blob-like content.
Central option-merging step for each request. It combines defaults and per-call input, merges query/params aliases, and produces resolved headers suitable for the fetch lifecycle.
Combines default headers and request-specific headers into a Headers object so per-request headers can override defaults. The graph shows resolveFetchOptions calling it.
Dispatches lifecycle hooks, supporting both single hook functions and arrays, awaited sequentially.
Node.js runtime adapter. It chooses native or polyfilled fetch behavior and optionally configures HTTP(S) keep-alive agents based on the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable.
Non-production example showing typed JSON response usage: fetch a repository record from ungh.cc and log its fields with generic typing.
Manual playground usage of the Node `$fetch` entrypoint against an HTTP error endpoint, demonstrating error logging/exit behavior. It is exploratory code, not core library behavior.
Test-only helper exercising abort behavior during a request configured with retries. It validates that aborted requests are rejected rather than retried in that scenario.

applicationFacts: `createFetch` is the central technical entity: the deterministic graph shows it calling `resolveFetchOptions`, `callHooks`, `isPayloadMethod`, `isJSONSerializable`, `onError`, and `detectResponseType`.
`resolveFetchOptions` calls `mergeHeaders`, indicating header merging is part of option resolution.
`onError` calls `isPayloadMethod` and `createFetchError`, showing retry policy is tied to HTTP body-method semantics and failures are normalized into FetchError objects.
Requests support automatic JSON body stringification and default JSON content-type/accept headers when the body is JSON-serializable.
Response parsing is driven by explicit `responseType`/`parseResponse` settings or inferred from Content-Type.
Retry defaults differ by method: the source treats payload methods as non-retryable by default and non-payload methods as retryable once unless configured.
Timeouts are implemented with an AbortController, and the code distinguishes active aborts from timeout-related aborts in retry logic.
The Node entrypoint can enable HTTP/HTTPS keep-alive agents via `FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE`.
Tests cover parsing, custom parsers, baseURL, query merging, body serialization, FormData/URLSearchParams passthrough, retries, timeouts, hooks, and error metadata.
